content.text:
**Finding: compliant** (no redline proposed).

The Agreement satisfies the **preferred** position for rule LD — no liquidated damages or penalties are payable by Ono.

Key points from the investigation:

- **Section 14.3 "Liquidated Damages" (p0668/p0671)** is the only LD clause, and it runs **in our favour**. It is triggered by *Array's* conduct — including intentional concealment or falsification of material safety/efficacy data undertaken to induce Ono not to terminate — and gives Ono the discretionary election to continue the Agreement, with relief from its own diligence obligations plus a reduction in the applicable royalty rate as the liquidated amount. Per the playbook, LDs payable by Vendor to Customer are compliant and are not flagged.
- **p0430** is a royalty true-up/reconciliation of amounts actually owed on Net Sales, not a stipulated penalty.
- **Section 7.1 (p0463)** is mutual, reciprocal late-payment interest at LIBOR plus a margin on genuinely overdue sums, payable by whichever Party is delinquent — compensatory interest, not liquidated damages.
- **No early-termination fee, minimum annual royalty, forfeiture, or minimum payment on termination** exists anywhere in the document. Section 14.5 confirms only already-accrued milestone and royalty payments survive.

Noted in the rationale but deliberately **not** flagged as a deviation: Sections 14.2(a)(i) and 14.2(a)(iii) shift the actual costs of wind-down transfers and ongoing Clinical Studies to Ono where Ono terminates for convenience under 13.2 or Array terminates for cause. These are uncapped reimbursements of genuine costs rather than a stipulated sum, so they are cost allocation and fall outside this rule — though they may be worth a look under any cost-allocation or termination-consequences rule if one exists in the playbook.
